title: Ab Wheel Rollout
summary: Roll a wheel out and back from the knees: abs 1, obliques 0.6. The abs work to stop the spine arching (anti-extension).

muscles.why: The rectus abdominis resists the spine arching as you roll out, then helps pull you back.
The lats pull the arms back to return: below the floor.
The spinal erectors stabilize: below the floor.

setup.text: Kneel on a pad, wheel under your shoulders.
Brace, slight round in the upper back.

form_cues.cue: Roll forward as far as you can hold a flat back
form_cues.why: Going only as far as you can return without arching.
Pulling back with the arms and abs.

form_cues.cue: Roll toward a wall to limit the range
form_cues.why: The wall stops you at a set distance while you build up.

bias_tweaks.caveat: Only if you can keep the back from arching.

mistakes.text: Letting the lower back sag at the far point.
mistakes.fix: Shorten the range until the back stays flat.

mistakes.text: Hips piking up first on the return.
mistakes.fix: Pull back with the abs and arms together.

misconceptions.reality: Training a muscle doesn't selectively reduce the fat over it.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.
There is no load to jump here: progress by adding reps, then range or a harder variation, one small step at a time.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Stop when you can't keep the back flat.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Loadable spinal flexion on a cable.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Bar only; curl the hips up.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Decline bench crunch with a plate.

notes: Ab exercises have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
